title_original: Gagosian to Sell Works from Mr. Chow’s Art Collection, Including Paintings by Warhol, Basquiat, Hockney, and More
editorial_title_zh: 高古轩将出售周英华艺术收藏中的作品，包括沃霍尔、巴斯奎特、大卫·霍克尼等人的画作
editorial_excerpt_zh: 就高古轩而言，他作为 Mr. Chow 的常客已经超过了 30 年。
editorial_blocks_json:
[{"type": "paragraph", "text": "拉里·高古轩（Larry Gagosian）几十年来一直在 Mr. Chow 招待艺术家、收藏家和各路名流。如今，他投桃报李，帮助他的老朋友迈克尔·周（Michael Chow，即周英华）出售一批多年来装点这位餐馆老板著名餐厅的精选艺术品。", "links": [{"text": "Larry Gagosian", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/larry-gagosian/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该画廊将呈现名为“朋友与传奇：迈克尔·周收藏”（Friends and Legends: The Collection of Michael Chow）的展览，展出周英华收藏中的 11 件作品，其中包括让-米歇尔·巴斯奎特、安迪·沃霍尔、大卫·霍克尼、凯斯·哈林、朱利安·施纳贝尔等艺术家为这位餐馆老板创作的肖像画。", "links": [{"text": "Andy Warhol", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/andy-warhol/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "参展的蓝筹大名极有可能出现在各大拍卖行即将到来的 11 月王牌晚拍中；据熟悉内情的消息人士透露，曾有一家拍卖行希望与周英华达成交易，但高古轩最终胜出。画廊未透露这些作品的价格，周英华也未就此时决定出售这些作品给出解释。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/BASQU_1985.0157_CRP.jpg?w=400", "alt": "", "caption": "让-米歇尔·巴斯奎特，《无题》，1985年。摄影：Josh White / ©让-米歇尔·巴斯奎特遗产管理委员会，经纽约 Artestar 授权 / 高古轩供图", "credit": "ARTnews", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览将于 11 月 4 日在高古轩的比弗利山庄画廊开幕，展期为 4 天，随后将移至高古轩位于纽约麦迪逊大道 980 号的新总部。第二部分展览将于 11 月 14 日开幕，正值该市秋季拍卖季拉开帷幕之际，并将持续至 12 月 22 日。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "对于一个很大程度上因友谊而诞生的收藏来说，这样的安排再合适不过了。周英华于 1968 年在伦敦骑士桥社区开办了他的第一家餐厅，随后于 1974 年在比弗利山庄、1979 年在纽约开店。在此过程中，Mr. Chow 几乎成了国际艺术界的非官方食堂。艺术家们在那里用餐，收藏家们在那里聚会，而本身也是艺术家的周英华则与当代艺术界的一些最大牌人物培养了友谊。其中许多友谊诞生了肖像画，有几幅已经在他的餐厅里悬挂了数十年。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "就高古轩而言，他作为这家高档餐厅的常客已经超过了 30 年。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "高古轩在声明中表示：“很难想到还有哪家餐厅比 Mr. Chow 更能让人联想到艺术界，”并补充说他认识周英华的时间比他在那里举办派对的时间还要长。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/BAL_3126412.jpg?w=400", "alt": "BBN3126412 安迪·沃霍尔在纽约 Mr Chow 与让-米歇尔·巴斯奎特、勒罗伊·内曼一起签署他的“荷兰豆”艺术品，1985年（黑白照片），布坎南（Buchanan, Ben）摄；（补充信息：让-米歇尔·巴斯奎特（1960-88）美国艺术家

请注意：Bridgeman Images 代表摄影师并为您清算版权。您的报价/发票中将增加一笔溢价费用。请联系 Bridgeman Images 了解详情。", "caption": "安迪·沃霍尔在纽约 Mr Chow 与让-米歇尔·巴斯奎特、勒罗伊·内曼一起签署他的“荷兰豆”艺术品，1985年。©2026 Ben Buchanan，保留所有权利", "credit": "ARTnews", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "参展作品中包括埃德·拉斯沙（Ed Ruscha）的《Mr. Chow L.A.》（1973年），该作品字面般地采用了餐厅的名字。拉斯沙使用厨房的原料创作了这幅画，包括蛋黄、大酱、甜菜根和椰奶。哈林也采取了一种烹饪的方法。他的《Mr. Chow as Green Prawns in a Bowl of Noodles》（1986年）描绘了三个版本的周英华游弋在餐厅招牌菜之一的各种配料之中。", "links": [{"text": "Ed Ruscha", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/t/ed-ruscha/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "沃霍尔的《迈克尔·周肖像》（1984年）通过覆盖着艺术家标志性钻石粉末的两块画屏展示了这位餐馆老板。沃霍尔的另一件作品是一面创作于 1959 年的折叠屏风，上面印有一幅甜点画和一个好玩的食谱，多年来一直矗立在比弗利山庄餐厅的甜点区附近。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴斯奎特于 1985 年绘制了周英华的肖像，据周英华回忆，这幅肖像在坐像创作过程中发生了出人意料的转变。“我为让-米歇尔做模特，”周英华在公告中回忆道。“他创作了这个强有力的形象，然后狂怒地在这幅画上进行涂抹，甚至没有看我和画布。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展出的还有彼得·布莱克、霍克尼和施纳贝尔的肖像画，其中施纳贝尔将餐厅里的碎盘子和精美瓷器融入了他的作品中。一件乌尔斯·菲舍尔（Urs Fischer）的蜡烛雕塑也将一同展出。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.artnews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/RUSCH_1973.0030_CRP.jpg?w=400", "alt": "一幅棕褐色调的画作，上面写着“MR. CHOW L.A.”", "caption": "埃德·拉斯沙，《Mr. Chow L.A.》，1973年。摄影：Josh White / ©Ed Ruscha / 高古轩供图", "credit": "ARTnews", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "有一件作品将包含更多艺术家的名字：一本《艺术家画册》（An Artist Drawing Book），里面写满了多年来客人们留下的绘画和题词。其贡献者包括弗朗西斯·培根、贾斯帕·约翰斯、赛·托姆布雷、路易丝·内维尔森、弗朗切斯科·克莱门特和马克·格罗蒂扬等人。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "周英华在声明中表示：“艺术和艺术家一直是我生活的核心。能够与这些珍宝共同生活并与公众分享它们，给我带来了巨大的快乐。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "至于他决定与之分道扬镳的决定，周英华给出了一个具有其标志性戏剧色彩的解释：“现在，是时候让他们走向世界，享受我自己的十五分钟成名时刻了。”", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Larry Gagosian has spent decades entertaining artists, collectors, and assorted celebrities at Mr. Chow. Now he’s returning the favor, helping his longtime friend Michael Chow sell a selection of artworks that have decorated the restaurateur’s famous dining rooms for years.

The gallery will present “Friends and Legends: The Collection of Michael Chow,” an exhibition of 11 works from Chow’s collection, including portraits of the restaurateur by Jean-Michel Basquiat, Andy Warhol , David Hockney, Keith Haring, Julian Schnabel, and more.

The blue-chip names on offer could easily feature in an evening sale for the auction houses’ upcoming November marquee sales; according to sources familiar with the sale, one house hoped to make a deal with Mr. Chow, but Gagosian won out. The gallery did not disclose prices for the works nor did Chow provide a reasoning for the decision to sell these works now.

The exhibition will open on November 4 at Gagosian’s Beverly Hills gallery, where it will run for four days before heading to the gallery’s new headquarters at 980 Madison Avenue in New York. The second installment opens November 14, just as the city’s fall auction season gets underway, and runs through December 22.

It’s a fitting arrangement for a collection that owes much of its existence to friendship. Chow opened his first restaurant in London’s Knightsbridge neighborhood in 1968, followed by Beverly Hills in 1974 and New York in 1979. Along the way, Mr. Chow became something of an unofficial dining room for the international art world. Artists ate there, collectors held court, and Chow, himself an artist, cultivated friendships with some of the biggest names in contemporary art. Many of those friendships produced portraits, several of which have hung in his restaurants for decades.

Gagosian, for his part, has been a regular at the high-end establishment for more than 30 years.

“It’s hard to think of a restaurant more synonymous with the art world than Mr. Chow,” Gagosian said in a statement, adding that he’d known Chow even longer than he’d been hosting parties there.

Among the works on offer is Ed Ruscha ‘s Mr. Chow L.A. (1973), which takes the restaurant’s name quite literally. Ruscha painted it using ingredients from the kitchen, including egg yolk, soybean paste, beets, and coconut milk. Haring also took a culinary approach. His Mr. Chow as Green Prawns in a Bowl of Noodles (1986) depicts three versions of Chow swimming among the ingredients of one of his restaurant’s signature dishes.

Warhol’s Portrait of Michael Chow (1984) shows the restaurateur across two panels coated in the artist’s trademark diamond dust. Another Warhol work, a folding screen from 1959 featuring a drawing of a dessert and a playful recipe, had for years stood near the dessert section of the Beverly Hills restaurant.

Basquiat painted Chow in 1985, producing a portrait that, according to Chow, took an unexpected turn during the sitting. “I sat for Jean-Michel,” Chow recalled in the announcement. “He made this powerful image and then ferociously painted over the picture without looking at me or the canvas.”

There are also portraits by Peter Blake, Hockney, and Schnabel, the last of whom incorporated broken plates and fine china from the restaurant into his work. An Urs Fischer candle sculpture will also be included.

One work will include the names of even more artists: An Artist Drawing Book , filled with drawings and inscriptions made by guests over the years. Its contributors include Francis Bacon, Jasper Johns, Cy Twombly, Louise Nevelson, Francesco Clemente, and Mark Grotjahn, among others.

“Art and artists have been at the heart of my life,” Chow said in a statement. “The privilege of living with these treasures and sharing them with the public has brought me great joy.”

As for his decision to part with them, Chow offered a characteristically theatrical explanation: “Now, it’s time to see them go out into the world and have my fifteen minutes.”
excerpt_original: Gagosian, for his part, has been a Mr. Chow regular for more than 30 years.

title_original: Richard Dadd’s Strange and Delicate Worlds
editorial_title_zh: 理查德·达德奇异而微妙的世界
editorial_excerpt_zh: 尽管他主要以其充满幻想的风景和神秘的林地生物作品而闻名，但一场全新的回顾展讲述了完整的故事。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "艺术评论", "links": [{"text": "Art Review", "url": "https://hyperallergic.com/tag/art-review/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "理查德·达德奇异而微妙的世界", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管他主要以其充满幻想的风景和神秘的林地生物作品而闻名，但一场全新的回顾展讲述了完整的故事。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/51/f8/51f871d8-b6be-4a73-b958-0ca4fff0110a/content/images/size/w1200/2026/10/Key-41-1.jpg", "alt": "理查德·达德奇异而微妙的世界", "caption": "", "credit": "Hyperallergic", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "伦敦——大多数英国观众知道理查德·达德都是通过《仙民伐木工的绝技》，该作品充满了对其主题的克制混乱以及对一名精神疾病患者不可避免的描绘。这件尺寸微小的作品现藏于泰特不列颠美术馆的永久收藏中，并在皇家艺术学院的回顾展《理查德·达德：超越贝特莱姆》中展出，创作于1855年至1864年间，并在达德被关押在贝特莱姆皇家医院期间被反复雕琢了近十年。这件作品布满了细节极其微小的幻想人物和仙子，在横贯画面的花朵与草叶之网下无限叠加。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "达德于1817年出生在英格兰查塔姆，活跃于维多利亚时代，曾在皇家艺术学院艺术学校学习。作为名为“The Clique”的艺术团体中的领军人才，他与其他英国艺术家（如奥古斯都·埃格和威廉·鲍威尔·弗里思）一同受到认可。但他的生平却被精神疾病所蒙上阴影，该病症最初在一次作为绘图员前往欧洲希腊、土耳其和叙利亚的远征中首次严重显现，并在1843年的一次妄洛发作中达到顶峰——当时他杀害了自己的父亲并逃往法国。在他被捕并被遣返回英国后，当局将他送入了贝特莱姆医院的刑事部。", "links": [{"text": "The Clique", "url": "https://www.tate.org.uk/art/art-terms/c/clique?ref=hyperallergic.com"}, {"text": "killed his own father and fled to France", "url": "https://hyperallergic.com/jennifer-higgies-empathetic-elegy-for-richard-dadd/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/51/f8/51f871d8-b6be-4a73-b958-0ca4fff0110a/content/images/2026/10/Key-59.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Hyperallergic", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "尽管他那细致入微、高度个性化的创作在很大程度上游离于历史正统之外，但皇家艺术学院明智地避免将他们对达德艺术生涯的全新综合调查视为“边缘艺术”（outsider art）。展览同样避免了心理学层面的解读，而是建议参观者前往贝特莱姆心灵博物馆（许多展品均借自该馆）了解关于达德在那里滞留的更多医学与历史细节。", "links": [{"text": "Bethlem Museum of the Mind,", "url": "https://museumofthemind.org.uk/?ref=hyperallergic.com"}], "translated": true}]
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "Art Review", "links": [{"text": "Art Review", "url": "https://hyperallergic.com/tag/art-review/"}]}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Richard Dadd’s Strange and Delicate Worlds"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Though he is known primarily for his work of fantastical landscapes and mystical woodland creatures, a new retrospective tells the full story."}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://storage.ghost.io/c/51/f8/51f871d8-b6be-4a73-b958-0ca4fff0110a/content/images/size/w1200/2026/10/Key-41-1.jpg", "alt": "Richard Dadd’s Strange and Delicate Worlds", "caption": "", "credit": "Hyperallergic"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "LONDON — Most British viewers know Richard Dadd from “The Fairy Feller’s Master-Stroke,” replete with its controlled chaos of subject matter and unavoidable depiction of a man suffering from mental illness. The diminutively scaled work, now in Tate Britain’s permanent collection and on view at the Royal Academy of Art’s retrospective exhibition, Richard Dadd: Beyond Bedlam , was painted between 1855 and 1864 and worked over repeatedly for nearly a decade while Dadd was incarcerated at Bethlem Royal Hospital. The work is filled with minutely detailed fantastical figures and fairies, overlaid ad infinitum under a web of flowers and grass blades that bisect its surface."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Dadd was born in 1817 in Chatham, England, worked during the Victorian era, and studied at the Royal Academy art schools. He was recognized as a leading talent among a group called The Clique , alongside other English artists such as Augustus Egg and William Powell Frith. But his biography is overshadowed by mental illness, which first became acutely evident on an expedition through Europe to Greece, Turkey, and Syria as a draftsman and culminated in a delusional episode in 1843 when he killed his own father and fled to France . article_text:
Art Review

Richard Dadd’s Strange and Delicate Worlds

Though he is known primarily for his work of fantastical landscapes and mystical woodland creatures, a new retrospective tells the full story.

LONDON — Most British viewers know Richard Dadd from “The Fairy Feller’s Master-Stroke,” replete with its controlled chaos of subject matter and unavoidable depiction of a man suffering from mental illness. The diminutively scaled work, now in Tate Britain’s permanent collection and on view at the Royal Academy of Art’s retrospective exhibition, Richard Dadd: Beyond Bedlam , was painted between 1855 and 1864 and worked over repeatedly for nearly a decade while Dadd was incarcerated at Bethlem Royal Hospital. The work is filled with minutely detailed fantastical figures and fairies, overlaid ad infinitum under a web of flowers and grass blades that bisect its surface.

Dadd was born in 1817 in Chatham, England, worked during the Victorian era, and studied at the Royal Academy art schools. He was recognized as a leading talent among a group called The Clique , alongside other English artists such as Augustus Egg and William Powell Frith. But his biography is overshadowed by mental illness, which first became acutely evident on an expedition through Europe to Greece, Turkey, and Syria as a draftsman and culminated in a delusional episode in 1843 when he killed his own father and fled to France . After his arrest and return to England, authorities committed him to Bethlem Hospital's criminal department.

Though his meticulously realized, highly individualized output sits largely outside the historical canon, the Royal Academy wisely avoids treating their new comprehensive survey of Dadd’s career as outsider art. The exhibition also avoids psychological interpretation and refers visitors to the Bethlem Museum of the Mind, from which many pieces have been loaned, for further medical and historical detail about Dadd’s stay there.

article_text:
We’re always talking about Stanley Kubrick around these parts. But lately, the “Shining” and “2001: A Space Odyssey” director is even more present in the cinephile conversation thanks to Criterion’s just-released, staggering box set covering Kubrick’s entire filmography. (Including the much-debated, rare international cut of “The Shining.”)

But also currently airing on podcast platforms is a new season of TCM host Ben Mankiewicz ‘s “ The Plot Thickens ,” an entire slate of episodes dedicated solely to the master filmmaker, who died in 1999 just before “ Eyes Wide Shut ” was released. IndieWire has some new exclusive news about the podcast: Two bonus episodes will be added to the already 11-episode run.

Turner Classic Movies has shared that it will release Stanley Kubrick’s rare, complete 1972 interview with Newsday film critic Joseph Gelmis as a bonus episode of “The Plot Thickens.” Available January 7, 2027, the episode presents the full conversation. So far, it’s only been excerpted across the season.

This “Clockwork Orange”-era interview “captures the famously private Kubrick in an expansive conversation with Gelmis, discussing his approach to directing actors and his beginnings as an independent filmmaker alongside personal interests, including football and his beloved pets,” per TCM.

In the episode, Kubrick also opines about a perennial cinephile topic: how home viewing might reshape moviegoing, even while advocating for the theatrical experience. While discussing “A Clockwork Orange,” Kubrick also recounts wearing a copper bracelet he believed relieved shoulder pain from playing ping-pong.

“Kubrick had a reputation for being private, but here you get to spend nearly three hours listening to him talk about his work and his everyday life,” said Ben Mankiewicz . “There’s pleasure in letting the conversation unfold; hearing what he takes seriously, what exasperates him, and what amuses him. What film lover isn’t curious about how Stanley Kubrick sees the world?”

Created in partnership with Criterion, the new “The Plot Thickens” season, “Stanley,” explores Kubrick’s life and career through archival audio and interviews with those who knew him and worked with him, with new episodes every Thursday.

TCM will also release a recording of its sold-out Kubrick panel presented in partnership with American Cinematheque at the Aero Theatre as an additional bonus episode on January 14, 2027. Moderated by Mankiewicz, the discussion features filmmaker Jason Reitman, dialect coach Elizabeth Himelstein, and former L.A. Times critic Kenneth Turan. The panel was held before a screening of “Dr. Strangelove.”

Both bonus episodes will be available on all major podcast apps and platforms, including Apple Podcasts, Spotify, and YouTube. Listen to our ”Screen Talk” podcast episode with Ben Mankiewicz , where he, along with co-hosts Anne Thompson and Ryan Lattanzio, ranks Kubrick’s top five films, here.

"translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在巴黎，我交谈过的一些画商对闭幕并不是特别在意。他们已经在贵宾日期间完成了销售，觉得没有理由去冒不必要的风险。豪瑟与沃斯（Hauser & Wirth）总裁马克·帕约（Marc Payot）告诉《金融时报》，他的画廊通常在艺博会早期就完成了大部分业务。但并非所有人的运营方式都像豪瑟与沃斯那样。", "links": [{"text": "Financial Times", "url": "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "纽约画商米格尔·阿布雷乌（Miguel Abreu）告诉我，他的画廊通常在最后两天完成约20%的艺博会业务。“人们在周末其实更有探索精神，”他说，“他们来的时候没有带着对什么是好东西、什么值得买的先入之见。”对于像他这样成熟的中型画廊来说，公众开放日是一个结识那些可能还不够了解艺术家、甚至对艺术市场了解不多的收藏家的机会。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "阿布雷乌理解周六闭幕的决定。周日则是另一回事，据消息人士称，在周日也被取消之前，并没有征求参展商的意见。目前尚不清楚巴塞尔艺术展是否或将如何对提前两天闭幕向画廊进行赔偿，不过消息人士告诉我，参展商正在组建一个松散的联盟，以要求艺博会给予某种形式的补偿。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴塞尔艺术展的一位发言人表示，周日继续闭展的决定是基于对示威活动可能持续的时间及其潜在影响的不确定性。该发言人称，主办方在决定提前闭展前已咨询了画廊、艺博会选委员会以及相关当局，不过并未明确周日是否曾被单独讨论。巴塞尔艺术展也正与参展商就可能的财务调整进行沟通，但尚未宣布任何具体措施。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "损失不仅限于画廊。巴塞尔艺术展正在退还未使用的周末门票，而餐厅、出租车司机以及艺博会本身的员工也失去了潜在的业务。即便每家画廊在周五之前就已经售罄所有作品，财务后果也不会仅仅止步于大皇宫（Grand Palais）的大门之外。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "保险经纪公司加利安（Gallagher）的国家美术业务负责人谢丽尔·卡里姆（Cheryl Karim）从事艺术品保险工作已有大约33年。她告诉我，画廊的保单可以包含针对无法追回的已记录费用的展会取消险，包括展位费、运输费、仓储费和差旅费。画廊还可以为单独的艺博会购买单独的险种，尽管条款差异很大。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "无法投保的是机会成本：即如果艺博会保持开放，某人可能会购买一幅画作的可能性。与传统零售商可能能够显示出可预测的月度收入不同，画廊很难证明在某个特定的周六下午本能卖出什么。保险单也无法取代那些从未走进门的收藏家与画廊之间的关系。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "卡里姆表示，尽管保险公司在评估艺博会时长期以来一直权衡地点、安保、交通和以往的中断情况，但在过去十年中，对恐怖主义保障的兴趣有所增加。她补充说，客户越来越清楚他们实际在为抵御什么风险购买保障。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "问题在于，画廊正越来越频繁地被要求承担这些风险。在售出第一件作品之前，一个艺博会的花费就可能高达数万甚至数十万美元。对于规模较小的企业来说，一次灾难性的参展经历可能很难恢复。连续几次则可能是毁灭性的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "迪拜艺术展（Art Dubai）提供了一个有趣的替代方案。在2月28日与伊朗爆发战争后，艺博会总监邓娅·戈特维斯（Dunja Gottweis）在咨询了参展商和收藏家后，将活动推迟至5月。画廊可以推迟到2027年且无需支付额外费用，或者无需预付展位费直接参加5月的展会，改为将销售额的一定比例交给主办方。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“这真的不是为了赚钱，”戈特维斯在迪拜通过电话对我说。“这纯粹是为了现身并支持我们的社群。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "该艺博会将这一理念延伸到了2027年的新参展商，他们将预付一半的展位费，其余部分则通过销售额提成支付。这是一个相对简单的改变，但这意味着主办方分担了一部分财务风险，而不是让画廊独自承担。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但还有一个与抗议活动、自然灾害或地缘政治毫无关系的问题：艺术圈的日程表正变得荒谬地拥挤。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "艺术顾问兼纯艺术集团（Fine Art Group）创始人菲利普·霍夫曼（Philip Hoffman）对这种层出不穷的活动日益感到沮丧。“现在有太多的艺博会在太短的时间内挤在一起，”他告诉我。他的团队不得不在纽约11月的拍卖会和同一时期举办的阿布扎比弗里兹艺博会（Frieze Abu Dhabi）之间做出选择。他们决定去纽约。", "links": [{"text": "Fine Art Group", "url": article_text:
Editor’s Note: This story originally appeared in On Balance , the ARTnews newsletter about the art market and beyond. Sign up here to receive it every Wednesday. On the Saturday before the opening of Art Basel Paris , two art professionals I’m friendly with found themselves trapped in a Paris metro station. Protesters were stampeding down the stairs, trailed by clouds of tear gas. They couldn’t see, could barely breathe, and struggled to find their way out. When they finally emerged onto the street a block or two away, people were sitting in restaurants, eating and drinking as though nothing had happened.

The contrast is almost comical, though I doubt anyone caught in the tear gas was laughing. One minute, you’re wondering whether you’ll make it out of a subway station. The next, someone is ordering another glass of bordeaux.

A few days later, the rest of the art world got its own reminder that the world doesn’t particularly care about its calendar.

Art Basel Paris, which had opened for its ultra-exclusive Avant-Première event last Tuesday, closed Friday evening, two days ahead of schedule, as organizers braced for a second weekend of demonstrations. Protests over education spending and inequality had already turned into rioting and looting the previous Saturday. Now activists were threatening to converge on the Grand Palais itself, where dealers were offering paintings worth tens of millions of dollars.

Closing was the sensible decision. Nobody wants to explain to an insurance company how a seven-figure Gerhard Richter ended up in the middle of a riot. But the decision also raised an uncomfortable question: What happens when an international art market built on gathering wealthy people in expensive places runs into a world that isn’t always hospitable?

It’s a question the industry might want to get used to answering.

Earlier this year, I was in Madrid when news broke that drones were being intercepted over Dubai following joint US and Israeli strikes on Iran. My wife called to tell me that, whatever plans I had to attend Art Dubai , I wouldn’t be going. I called a friend in the city to see how things were. She was at the beach.

The art market has become very good at carrying on with business. Over the past three decades, it has grown into an enormous circuit of fairs, auctions, gallery openings, and biennials, supported by dealers, collectors, advisers, shippers, insurers, and people who seem to spend more time in airport lounges than at home.

For years, that growth was treated as an unqualified good. More fairs meant more collectors, more opportunities for galleries, and, at least in theory, a more international and democratic art market. But globalization works both ways. If you’re going to do business everywhere, you’re going to encounter everything that happens everywhere, too.

Art Basel Miami Beach was supposed to debut in December 2001, but the September 11 attacks forced organizers to postpone the inaugural edition until 2002. In 2015, Paris Photo closed early after the coordinated terrorist attacks across Paris, including at the Bataclan concert hall, that killed 130 people. And in March 2020, TEFAF Maastricht became one of the art world’s early Covid horror stories. The fair closed four days early after an exhibitor tested positive, and later reporting by The Art Newspaper identified more than 25 cases among attendees and exhibitors. Two years later, the fair was robbed .

Sometimes organizers decide the show must go on.

After devastating wildfires swept through Los Angeles in January 2025, Frieze insisted that its Los Angeles fair would go ahead in February, arguing that bringing collectors and galleries to the city would help support the local arts community. It was an understandable position, though there was something uncomfortable about an international art fair being presented as a community-building exercise while parts of the city were still recovering from disaster.

There’s no obvious rule for these situations. Cancel a fair, and galleries lose business. Hold it, and you risk appearing indifferent to what’s happening outside. Either way, someone’s going to be unhappy.

In Paris, some dealers I spoke to weren’t particularly bothered by the closure. They’d already made their sales during the VIP days and saw little reason to take unnecessary risks. Marc Payot , president of Hauser & Wirth, told the Financial Times that his gallery generally does most of its business early in the fair. But not everyone operates like Hauser & Wirth.

New York dealer Miguel Abreu told me that his gallery typically does about 20 percent of its fair business during the final two days. “People are actually more explorative on the weekends,” he said. “They don’t come in with preconceptions of what’s what and what’s worth buying or not.” For an established midsize gallery like his, the public days are a chance to meet collectors who might not already know the artists, or even much about the art market.

Abreu understood the decision to close on Saturday. Sunday was another matter, and sources say exhibitors weren’t consulted before that day was canceled, too. It’s unclear whether or how Art Basel will compensate galleries for closing two days early, though sources tell me a loose coalition of exhibitors is forming to ask the fair for some kind of restitution.

An Art Basel spokesperson said the decision to remain closed Sunday was based on uncertainty about how long the demonstrations might last and their potential impact. The spokesperson said organizers had consulted galleries, the fair’s Selection Committee, and authorities about the early closure, though didn’t specify whether Sunday had been discussed separately. Art Basel is also speaking with exhibitors about possible financial accommodations, but hasn’t announced any measures.

The costs extend beyond the galleries. Art Basel is refunding unused weekend tickets, while restaurants, cabdrivers, and workers at the fair itself lost potential business. Even if every dealer had sold everything by Friday, the financial consequences wouldn’t have stopped at the doors of the Grand Palais.

Cheryl Karim , national fine arts practice leader at the insurance broker Gallagher, has worked in art insurance for some 33 years. She told me that gallery policies can include event-cancellation coverage for documented expenses that can’t be recovered, including booth fees, shipping, storage, and travel. Galleries can also buy separate coverage for individual fairs, although the terms vary considerably.

What can’t be insured is opportunity cost: the possibility that someone might have bought a painting had the fair stayed open. Unlike a conventional retailer, which might be able to show predictable monthly revenue, a gallery can’t easily prove what would have sold on a particular Saturday afternoon. Nor can an insurance policy replace a relationship with a collector who never walked through the door.

Karim said interest in terrorism coverage has increased over the past decade, although insurers have long weighed location, security, transportation, and previous disruptions when evaluating fairs. Clients, she added, are becoming more conscious of what they’re actually buying protection against.

The trouble is that galleries are being asked to take these risks more and more often. A fair can cost tens or even hundreds of thousands of dollars before a single work sells. For a smaller business, one disastrous outing can be difficult to recover from. Several in a row can be ruinous.

Art Dubai offers an interesting alternative. After war broke out with Iran on February 28, fair director Dunja Gottweis consulted exhibitors and collectors before postponing the event until May. Galleries could defer until 2027 without additional fees or take part in May without paying booth fees upfront, instead giving organizers a percentage of sales.

“This was really not about making money,” Gottweis told me by phone from Dubai. “This was just to show up and support our community.”

The fair is extending the idea to new exhibitors in 2027, who will pay half their booth fee upfront and the remainder through a percentage of sales. It’s a relatively simple change, but it means organizers share some of the financial risk rather than leaving dealers to shoulder it alone.

But there’s another problem that has nothing to do with protests, natural disasters, or geopolitics: The art world calendar is becoming absurdly crowded.

Philip Hoffman , the art adviser and founder of the Fine Art Group , has grown increasingly frustrated with the relentless string of events. “Right now there are too many fairs crammed into too little time,” he told me. His team has to choose between the November auctions in New York and Frieze Abu Dhabi, which falls during the same period. They’re going to New York.

“I physically can’t get to two places on the same day,” he said.

It’s an obvious limitation, but one the art market seems determined to test. The assumption that collectors, advisers, and galleries can keep adding destinations to their calendars starts to look rather optimistic when even the people with the money and the inclination to travel can’t keep up.

As for geopolitics, Hoffman doesn’t believe instability or civil unrest necessarily discourages collectors from visiting a country, provided they can get in and out safely. The international art market isn’t about to abandon Dubai or Paris because of one difficult year, nor should it.

But Gottweis offered a useful warning to galleries that depend too heavily on a handful of fairs. “It’s dangerous to put all your eggs in one basket and have your business depend on sales during one week. I don’t think the current world is supporting this so much.”

She’s probably right.

None of this means that the art market should stop expanding. Growth outside New York, London, and Switzerland has created opportunities for artists, galleries, and collectors who might otherwise have been left out. Whether that amounts to democratization is another question, especially when the price of admission remains so high.

But an industry that prides itself on its international reach ought to be prepared for the consequences. The world outside the fairgrounds isn’t always peaceful, predictable, or particularly interested in the needs of the art trade. Sometimes it’s at war. Sometimes it’s protesting. Sometimes it’s on fire.

And sometimes, despite all the champagne, business-class flights, hotel suites, and institutional galas, the outside world finds its way inside. The art market wanted to be everywhere. It just hadn’t counted on everything else being there, too.

article_text:
Art Basel Qatar is returning for its sophomore edition from January 28 to 30 to three venues in Msheireb Downtown Doha : Barahat Msheireb, M7, and Doha Design District. The fair features 82 galleries from 37 countries, with 50 percent of the artists hailing from the Middle East, North Africa, and South Asia, while more than a third of the participating galleries operate within these regions.

The fair has teamed with Qatar Sports Investments (QSI), QC+, and Visit Qatar as official partners to “deepen collector relationships, support galleries, and sustain momentum between editions.” This month, a program called “Collectors Majlis” will be introduced to local and international collectors, galleries, and institutions to engage them in the arts; the initiative includes master classes, workshops, invitation-led community encounters, cultural experiences, collection visits, and more.

The theme of the 2027 edition of Art Basel Qatar is “between” and was conceived by Iraqi artistic director Wassan Al-Khudhairi , who in May was announced to lead the fair into its second chapter. “For me, the theme between is a liminal space of possibility, where different perspectives, histories and ideas meet and new ways of seeing emerge,” said Al-Khudhairi in a statement. She added that the aim was to bring “together artists across generations and at different stages of their careers.” Al-Khudhairi has also been collaborating with Vincenzo de Bellis, chief artistic officer and global director of fairs at Art Basel. Like last year, each gallery’s booth will feature a solo presentation.

Galleries from the region, such as Efie Gallery (Dubai), Iyad Qanazea (Abu Dhabi), Le LAB Gallery (Giza), Alhosh Gallery (Doha), Contemporary Art Platform (Kuwait), and Dastan Gallery (Tehran, Toronto) will be participating in their first Art Basel Qatar fair, joining the likes of Sprüth Magers (Berlin), Lisson Gallery (London), White Cube (London), The Breeder (Athens), David Zwirner (New York), Gagosian (New York), and Sadie Coles HQ (London).

Art Basel outlined that it would be offering galleries the same support as it did with the inaugural edition, this includes customs clearance, in-country transportation, consolidated storage and installation services, hotel accommodation for up to two staff members, and travel and hotel costs for exhibiting artists. The fair is also offering covering 50 percent of outbound shipping costs for unsold works and up to a maximum of $20,000 per gallery. The fair has put these initiatives into place to provide participating galleries flexibility with cost control and reflect Art Basel’s “commitment to supporting galleries and contributing to the long-term development of the art market in the region.”

Art Basel Qatar, like fairs such as Frieze London and Art Basel Paris, will coincide with various exhibitions taking place in Qatar, including “What Lingers in the Artist Mind: Experiments and Legacies of the Baghdad Modern Art Group” at Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art until February 6, 2027, and “Bu’ed Nadhar” at Liwan Design Studios and Labs, through January 31, 2027.

article_text:
2026年10月28日、韓国国立現代美術館（MMCA）は、SBS財団と共催する韓国国内有数の現代美術賞「韓国美術家賞（今年の作家賞）」を、ホン・ジンフォンに授賞すると発表した。ホンには賞金1000万ウォン（約120万円）が授与された（※最終候補の4名には最終のプレゼンテーションとなる展覧会の新作製作補助費として5000万ウォンが提供されている）。

ホン・ジンフォン （1980年生まれ）は、写真や映像、ウェブプログラミングなどを活用し、イメージに埋め込まれた社会的・政治的な権力構造について探究している。国際的な報道メディアでジャーナリストとして働いた経験を背景に、彼自身が目撃してきた抗議運動の現場がどのようにイメージへと変換されるのかに着目し、異なるイメージやサウンドを並置することにより、その中で作用する権力構造への介入を試みてきた。

新作《The Highest Form of the Image Is Armed Struggle（イメージは最良の形態は武装闘争である）》（2026）では、足立正生と若松孝二が『赤軍-PFLP・世界戦争宣言』内で掲げたスローガン「プロパガンダの最良の形態は武装闘争である」を、現代の抗議運動の風景の中に探りつつ、抵抗と闘争の場が予測可能で制御可能なイメージへと変容していく過程を、動物学者ジョン・B・カルフーンの実験「ユニバース25」と結びつけながら考察している。また、《Exactly Speaking, the Milky Way Is a Phantom（正確に言えば、銀河は亡霊である）》（2026）では、銀河を無数の星の分布とそれを観測する視線の関係の中で形成されるイメージとして捉えたオランダの天文学者アントン・パネコックの研究を引き合いに、ホン自身が撮影してきた悲劇を経験した場所の風景写真を観測と記憶の中でのみ現れる亡霊的なイメージとして提示することで、不在と沈黙、凝視と記憶の問題を問い直した。 審査員を務めたテート・モダンのシャーメーン・トーは、「ホン・ジンフォンの作品は、社会的実践とそれらがイメージとして表象される過程との間にある緊張関係を明らかにし、私たちが現実を見る、理解する際の視覚体系に疑問を投げかけている」と評し、同じく審査員を務めたベルリンのクンストヴェルケ現代美術センターのエマ・エンダービーは、「異なる時代、異なる文脈のイメージや記録の編み込み方が印象的で、社会的な出来事を伝え、その意味を再構築するイメージの作用を説得的に示している」と言及した。 また、韓国国立現代美術館ディレクター代理のユン・テウクは、「ホン・ジンフォンは、イメージが単に現実を記録する手段に留まらず、社会的な出来事の意味や記憶を構成する本質的な条件なのだということを示し、私たちが慣れ親しんできた視覚体系と権力関係について再考を促しました」とグランプリを受賞したホンを賞賛した上で、「展覧会を通じて、韓国現代美術の卓越した力量を証明してくれた4名の最終候補者に感謝の意を表します」と展覧会に参加したすべてのアーティストを讃えた。

本年度の審査員は、上述したトー、エンダービーのほか、ホー・ツーニェン（第16回光州ビエンナーレ アーティスティックディレクター）、チョン・ヒョン（美術批評家、仁荷大学校教授）、キム・ジヨン（d/pディレクター）、キム・ソンヒ（韓国国立現代美術館ディレクター）が務めた。受賞者は、10月27日に開かれた観客参加型座談会を経て、審査員による非公開の最終審査を通じて選定された。 最終候補4名の作品を紹介する「韓国美術家賞2026」は、12月6日まで韓国国立現代美術館 ソウル館で開催。なお、受賞者のホン・ジンフォンの過去作《オー・バレンタイン》は、 イメージフォーラム・フェスティバル2026 の東アジア・エクスペリメンタル・コンペティションの出品作品に選ばれており、同フェスティバルの名古屋会場のナゴヤキネマ・ノイでも11月12日に上映予定となっている。

article_text:
Long Long Night (2026) by Youm Kyu-bock Film Review

From Ru Ri’s bestseller, an animated coming-of-age journey through fatherhood and grief, with the voices of Park Ki-wook and Suzy

The only animated film in the competition section of the 31st Busan International Film Festival, Youm Kyu-bock’s “Long Long Night” is based on the book of the same name by Ru Ri, a celebrated tale with over 800,000 copies sold. Director Youm approached the story together with his daughter. The book had already inspired a musical and a pansori version, so bringing it to the big screen was, as the director himself rightly pointed out, a truly long night .

Long Long Night is screening at Busan International Film Festival

The film arrives after some very famous productions, and it won’t be hard to feel transported to the landscapes of “Flow”, the Latvian hit of 2024, or to recall the humor of the penguins in “Madagascar”, the DreamWorks franchise with fans all over the world. Here too, the penguins are hilarious.

The film features the voices of Kim Kyu-na and Suzy, who bring the little penguin to life, while Park Ki-wook, with his dense timbre, voices Norden.

The story is very simple and moving but never loses its cheerfulness, and follows the unusual life of Norden, a white rhino rescued from poachers and taken to an elephant reserve, where he learns, first of all, how to be an elephant. Just as he nestles into what he believes is his world, he is offered the freedom and the identity that are rightfully his. Running “faster than the wind,” he meets another white rhino and, with her, a family. The last of their kind.

Once again, just when he thinks he has found happiness, a tragedy forces him back into solitude and confinement. Norden is transported to a zoo and manages to escape only because war breaks out among his own jailers, who are, of course, human beings. Having survived, he sets off once more, this time with Chiku, a grumpy penguin who walks carrying a precious bucket in his beak, in which he keeps his egg, still waiting to hatch. When the egg hatches, the second part of the film begins: the second, greater voyage of Norden and the newborn, toward the sea.

“Long Long Night” is an animation made with contemporary techniques, namely Unreal Engine, a video game graphics engine, much lighter and cheaper than better-known animation software such as Maya. If technically it is an experimental undertaking, from a narrative standpoint, the film follows a classic arc. The hero’s journey, as Campbell would have it.

And yet Norden is not a traditional hero. He is a survivor, who processes multiple traumas and who channels his mission into fatherhood. It is touching to consider how closely the “Long Long Night” project itself aligns with the film’s theme, since it was born from a father (the director himself) reading a story to his daughter. That bond and the theme of parenthood find an echo in the characters who, animated though they are, show an emotional depth that leaves no one indifferent.

The film is neatly divided into sequences, or perhaps it is better to say into stages of life: youth, adulthood and old age. Norden matures through his experiences, which, once acquired, are ready to be passed on. Even to a penguin. This blend of species nods to unconventional families, and the solutions the film proposes are plainly, lovingly successful.

There is nothing this rhino won’t come up with to make the penguin appreciate his “penguinness” and to nurture in him the desire to reach an ocean he has never seen, but toward which he must head all the same. Norden wields the magic of storytelling, which educates, reassures, comforts and energizes. It is a poetic dynamic that points back to cinema itself: a film about the power of stories, folding back on itself. We are both outside and inside the screen without even knowing it.

Drawing on the freedom the digital environment has given him, Youm Kyu-bock plays festively with the action scenes. He doesn’t necessarily make the film adrenaline-fueled; he offers them as fitting entertainment for the viewer. A herd of wildebeest migrates, enraged and out of control, and not even a rhino can withstand its force. From this pitiless surge comes a thrilling scene in the waters of a raging river, where a rhino father’s desperation becomes the will to survive. It is also the scene where the software’s technical limits, especially in the rendering of water, are most visible, though in the emotional whirlwind they vanish.

The director deliberately chooses not to describe certain moments precisely: the protagonist’s thoughts, most of the time reserved and taciturn, are told by the starry sky. Likewise, some memories and emotions return and are reworked as bedtime stories. “Long Long Night” is truly rich in ideas that are not handed over gratuitously but revealed gradually. It allows us to embrace the natural course of loss and to accept the impermanence of existence, though not without a few tears. Vulnerabilities evolve into acceptance and perseverance, thus revealing themselves as strength.

Confident in his background in advertising, Youm Kyu-bock cuts the film at a frenetic rhythm where needed and slows it down when we need rest, a gathered, introspective moment. This wise alternation fosters the fullest immersion in, and involvement with, the challenges Norden and his extended family face.

It is a family film, and one that draws viewers toward the environmental cause without growing rigid on the theme. Above all, it breathes infinite landscapes, saturated colors and long shots, daring point-of-view shots and carefully worked details, not so common in traditional animation. Purists will notice a certain “robotic” stiffness in the movements and video-game pacing. But in front of a rhino teaching a penguin to believe in an ocean he has never seen, that detail can be overlooked.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Established streaming platform Plex has teamed up with Fandango to allow U.S. users to find showtimes and buy movie tickets as they browse and watch films.

Founded in 2011, Plex offers a suite of streaming options from free, ad-supported live and on-demand programming to transactional VOD. Its discovery and community efforts have enabled the company to hold its own in a streaming world dominated by Roku, Amazon and other large-scale players. It operates in more than 180 countries and has more than 42 million monthly active users.

Fandango has branched out from its origins under current owner Versant, adding general-entertainment streaming and other offerings, but it remains the leading online movie ticket seller.

Related Stories

Peter Rice Will Blend "Art And Commerce" In Heading Content For Netflix, Ted Sarandos Says

Netflix Stock Falls Despite Solid Q3 Results On Lowered Advertising Guidance, Disappointing Revenue Outlook

Especially as moviegoing has rebounded after Covid, a number of streamers have looked to unite the small and big screens in various ways. Roku in 2025 added a “coming soon to theaters” feature to its user experience, but it stopped short of enabling ticket purchases.

Watch on Deadline

Under the partnership, which lit up this week, Plex users in the U.S. will see a Fandango ticketing option on title pages for movies that are currently playing in theaters. The feature lets them click through to Fandango to find showtimes and buy tickets. The integration also includes direct attribution through measurement firm Kochava, which promises to give studios and advertisers greater visibility into how campaigns and audience engagement translate into ticket sales.

As more of streaming has shifted toward advertising over the past few years, with all major streamers except Apple TV making it a major strategic focus, there has also been an increased emphasis on outcomes. In other words, knowing how ads prompt purchase decisions is even more of a brass ring than ever.

The Letterboxd-like community aspect of Plex is a key element in the partnership. More than 45 million users create watchlists, the company says, giving it an advantage in terms of content discovery in a marketplace where average viewers struggle to find films and series of interest.

“Our vision is to make Plex the place where people can discover what to watch, regardless of where that content lives. Fandango lets us extend that experience to all theatrical releases in the U.S., giving fans an easy way to act once they find a movie they want to see,” Scott Olechowski, co-founder and chief product officer of Plex, said in a statement.

“Plex has a unique view into what movie fans are actively considering, from what they’re searching for to what they’re watching across services,” said Jerramy Hainline, EVP of Fandango. “By connecting those discovery signals with Fandango ticketing, we’re making it easier for fans to turn that interest into a trip to the theater, while giving studios and advertisers a more direct, measurable path to ticket sales.”

article_text:
Editor’s Note: This review was originally published during the 2026 Sundance Film Festival. “ Soul Patrol ” opens in select theaters from Kino Lorber starting Friday, November 6.

The Vietnam War ended over a half-century ago, but the 20-year war remains a conflict that American artists keep going back to, finding new avenues and perspectives to tackle the many stories of the generation of men who had their lives irrevocably shaped by the conflict. Recent takes have centered the (often-neglected) perspective of the Vietnamese, or — like Spike Lee’s underrated late-career great “Da 5 Bloods” — explored the relatively under-examined service of Black men who served in the war.

“Soul Patrol,” a new documentary from director J.M. Harper, looks at the Black soldiers of the war through the perspective of Ed Emanuel, a writer who served as a 17-year-old. In his 2003 memoir of the same title, Emanuel described tracking down and reuniting with the men he served with in the first Black special operations Long-Range Reconnaissance Patrol team, during his short 1968 to 1969 tour.

“Soul Patrol” finds the men in 2024, in what will be the last reunion they hold. Gathering together, the men — Emanuel, Lawton Mackey, Thad Givens, Emerson Branch, Jesse Lewis, Willie T. Brown, Willie Merkerson, and Norman Reid — sit in the conference room of a Florida hotel to discuss the memories of their service that has stuck with them over the decades, in the hope that their discussion can help them move on.

The opening, and Emmanuel’s narration, help bring context to the small stretch of the war that the film explores. In 1968, as the young men went to serve their country, America itself proved more turbulent than ever; Emanuel was on the plane to Vietnam as Robert F. Kennedy’s assassination was first reported. Protests against the war were growing, and the Civil Rights movement opposed the war as well; a speech from Martin Luther King Jr. becomes a crucial emotional turning point for Emanuel later, as he begins to wonder whether the trauma he experienced serving in the war was worth it.

Through the film, Emanuel and the footage of the reunion between the men guide the audience through their experiences, from the trauma they endured to the discrimination and tokenization they faced as Black soldiers fighting for America. One scene peels back at the men’s conflicting feelings around the nickname for their unit, a racialized moniker that’s simultaneously endearing and patronizing. Others focus on formative experiences Emanuel experiences throughout the war, including a hazy night in Bangkok that’s proves formative both sexually and emotionally.

Harper — whose debut feature “As We Speak” also played at Sundance — has a loud, uncompromisingly blunt style, and the film missteps most clearly when his directorial choices verge on heavy-handed. The film makes clumsy use of actor-led reenactments that are a little too slick and generic to slot seamlessly into the Super 8 footage and actor interviews that make up the bulk of the story. This particularly applies to an opening visual metaphor, in which an old veteran is haunted by a vision of his past, which proves more excessive and obvious than enlightening. Other formal choices feel designed to provoke emotional reactions the material can easily do on its own, particularly a loud, string-heavy score that feels overly generic for the material.

It’s when the film mostly gets out of its own way and lets the men’s experiences do the work that “Soul Patrol” really shines. The Super 8 footage collected from their tour in Vietnam, most of which was shot by the men themselves, is visually arresting and intimate, and Harper frequently employs quick cuts and montages of that on-the-ground film and b-roll of newscasts and ads of the time to flesh out the world they once inhabited. The reunion scenes are simply but artfully shot in black and white, including a revealing conversation among the men’s wives and partners about living with them that gently broadens the perspectives in the film’s portrait.

“Soul Patrol” admirably never tries to sum up the full experience of what Vietnam was, rather just trying to sum up what it was for these men. In the film’s closing stretch, it turns its attention to the men’s difficult experiences returning home from the war, with a candor and a vulnerability that’s hard not to tear up from. As one member of Soul Patrol reflects eloquently towards the end of the film, “We need to tell the stories to look at where we were at, where we come from, and where we headed. You need to know your beginning before you can figure out your ending.”

Grade: B

“Soul Patrol” premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival. Kino Lorber opens the film in select theaters starting Friday, November 6.

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "当语言不再仅仅是一种交流工具，而成为一个被边界、禁令、归属感和可能性所穿越的地方时，会发生什么？这是Shilpa Gupta研究中伴随的一个问题，这位印度艺术家是国际当代艺术界最具权威的声音之一，是米兰GAM——现代艺术画廊第八届Furla Series的主角。Gupta在过去二十年里一直在探索社会构建和规范身份的一些装置。语言、审查、流动性、边界和个体自由贯穿她的实践，根据所面对的问题，她的作品形式不断变化。雕塑、灯光装置、视频、声音和表演作为观察个体与集体、私人体验与公共空间之间关系的工具。她的作品正是在这些维度重叠的地方诞生，即一个词、一幅图像或一个动作在不同地方被说出或展示时可能具有不同意义的区域。", "links": [{"text": "Furla Series", "url": "https://www.fondazionefurla.org/"}, {"text": "GAM – Galleria d’Arte Moderna", "url": "https://www.gam-milano.com/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Shilpa-Gupta-2-853x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Furla Series – Shilpa Gupta。One Palm Closer to the Sky，2026。由Fondazione Furla和GAM——米兰现代艺术画廊举办的展览现场。摄影：Andrea Rossetti。版权：Fondazione Furla", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在GAM，这种研究与一座历史悠久的建筑和永久收藏品展开对话，这种对比催生了一系列专门为博物馆空间创作的新作品，这些空间位于美丽的皇家别墅花园中。该项目因此将一系列作品带到米兰，这些作品概括了Gupta实践中的核心主题，构建了一条将环境维度提升为艺术体验不可或缺部分的路线。一件名为《I Live Under Your Sky Too》的作品，始于2004年，至今仍在进行中，仅从标题就能体现出艺术家研究中反复出现的张力。一句简单、几乎日常的话语引出了归属感和共存的问题：共享同一片天空是否真的意味着共享同一片空间、同样的权利、同样的行动自由和被认可的可能性？Gupta经常探讨这种看似普遍与实际限制之间的差距。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Shilpa-Gupta-3-683x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Furla Series – Shilpa Gupta. One Palm Closer to the Sky, 2026. 由Fondazione Furla和GAM – 米兰现代艺术画廊共同举办的展览现场照片。Ph. Andrea Rossetti。版权所有 Fondazione Furla", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "语言因此成为一种需要检验的材料。词语可以穿越领土，创造社区，标记差异，但也可以成为控制的工具。审查不仅涉及明确禁止的内容，还涉及社会如何规定什么可以被说、由谁说、用哪种语言以及在何种空间中说。这是Gupta研究中特别深入探讨的领域，她将不同的语言和地理联系在一起，而不将政治维度与个人维度分开。展览开始的房间在这方面具有象征意义。一件特定场地的声景装置，由石头、家具和回收的玻璃杯制成，将房间的复制品转化为一个共鸣箱。《When the Stone Sang to the Glass》被转化为“Bella Ciao”的合唱版和低语版，将参观者带入印度艺术家的艺术和政治视野。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "展览继续以名为《Truth》的霓虹灯装置展开，其中文字被倒置。古普塔将观众的注意力引向当下的矛盾，以及当代社会面临的极权主义威胁和日益加剧的专制倾向。在这一背景下，艺术家探讨了审查制度、语言的核心地位以及政府对媒体的控制，她通过《SoundOnMySkin》等作品，以旋转字母的显示屏来呈现，这些作品摒弃了作为提供清晰信息媒介的常规角色，反而提供混乱且脱节的句子。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Shilpa-Gupta-5-1024x683.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Furla Series – Shilpa Gupta. One Palm Closer to the Sky, 2026. 由Fondazione Furla和GAM – 米兰现代艺术画廊共同举办的展览现场。Ph. Andrea Rossetti。版权所有 Fondazione Furla", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在两件作品中，语言成为被审视的对象。这是民主的第一道防线，如今更是被政府和政权用作引导日益疲惫的民众的工具。在展览中还包括互动装置如《Stand, Speak, Here》（2026年创作）和《Breathe》，通过不同的方式邀请参观者直接与之互动。前者鼓励参观者站在砖块上并闭上嘴唇发出声音，这明显影射了政治言论中对异议的边缘化和镇压。后者则邀请参观者采取行动，他们可以将一张纸放在博物馆墙壁上艺术家刻下的凹痕上，然后用粉笔拓印。在这些刻痕中，很快就能注意到被逮捕示威者的缺失。古普塔故意只展示执法者或暴徒的形象，而异议者的轮廓则仅通过他们缺席的回声显现出来。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/Shilpa-Gupta-6-683x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Furla Series – Shilpa Gupta. One Palm Closer to the Sky, 2026. 由Fondazione Furla和GAM – 米兰现代艺术画廊共同举办的展览现场。Ph. Andrea Rossetti。版权所有 Fondazione Furla", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "GAM的项目是在2021年起，Fondazione Furla与米兰博物馆之间建立的合作关系中诞生的。每年，这种合作都会推出一场全新的展览，旨在让一位当代艺术家的研究与GAM的历史环境和其收藏进行对话。这种对比使人们能够通过时间与文化上的距离来审视这些作品，这些距离将它们与博物馆中保存的作品分隔开来。Furla Series由Fondazione Furla于2017年启动，并与意大利重要的艺术机构合作，已举办了来自世界各地女性艺术家的个人展览，并为当代文化中的女性主角提供了可见度。此次在米兰与Shilpa Gupta的相遇，是其国际广泛艺术研究的一部分。从威尼斯双年展到柏林、沙迦、利物浦和光州双年展，再到欧洲、亚洲和美国博物馆的展览，这位艺术家的作品跨越了不同的语境，始终将个体、领土和权力结构之间的关系作为核心。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Cosa accade quando il linguaggio smette di essere soltanto uno strumento per comunicare e diventa un luogo attraversato da confini, divieti, appartenenze e possibilità? È una delle domande che accompagnano la ricerca di Shilpa Gupta , artista indiana tra le voci più autorevoli della scena contemporanea internazionale, protagonista dell’ottava edizione di Furla Series alla GAM – Galleria d’Arte Moderna di Milano. Gupta lavora da oltre vent’anni su alcuni dei dispositivi attraverso cui le società costruiscono e regolano l’identità. Linguaggio, censura, mobilità, confini e libertà individuale attraversano una pratica che cambia forma a seconda delle domande affrontate. Sculture, installazioni luminose, video, suono e performance fungono da strumenti per osservare il rapporto tra individuo e collettività, esperienza privata e spazio pubblico. Il suo lavoro nasce proprio dove queste dimensioni si sovrappongono, in quella zona in cui una parola, un’immagine o un gesto possono assumere significati diversi a seconda del luogo in cui vengono pronunciati o mostrati.

Alla GAM, questa ricerca viene messa in dialogo con un edificio storico e una collezione permanente, un confronto che ha dato origine a una serie di nuove produzioni realizzate appositamente per gli spazi del museo sito negli splendidi Giardini della Villa Reale. Il progetto porta dunque a Milano una selezione di opere che sintetizza alcuni dei nuclei centrali della pratica di Gupta , costruendo un percorso in cui la dimensione ambientale viene elevata a parte integrante dell’esperienza artistica. Un’opera come I Live Under Your Sky Too , iniziata nel 2004 e tuttora in corso, restituisce già nel titolo una delle tensioni ricorrenti nella ricerca dell’artista. Una frase semplice, quasi quotidiana, introduce una questione di appartenenza e convivenza: condividere lo stesso cielo vuole dire davvero condividere lo stesso spazio, gli stessi diritti, la stessa possibilità di muoversi e di essere riconosciuti? Gupta lavora spesso proprio su questo scarto tra ciò che appare come universale e le condizioni concrete che ne limitano l’accesso.

Il linguaggio si fa così materia da mettere alla prova. Le parole possono attraversare territori, creare comunità, segnare differenze, ma anche diventare strumenti di controllo. La censura riguarda sia ciò che viene esplicitamente proibito ma anche i modi in cui una società stabilisce cosa può essere detto, da chi, in quale lingua e in quale spazio. È un terreno particolarmente sondato nella ricerca di Gupta , che mette in relazione lingue e geografie diverse senza separare la dimensione politica da quella intima. La sala che apre la mostra è in questo senso emblematica. Un’installazione sonora site-specific, realizzata con pietre, arredi e bicchieri di recupero trasforma la riproduzione di una stanza in una cassa di risonanza. When the Stone Sang to the Glass si traduce in una versione corale e sussurrata di “Bella Ciao” che proietta il visitatore nella visione artistica e politica dell’artista indiana.

La mostra prosegue con l’installazione Truth , neon in cui la scritta viene rovesciata. Gupta porta all’attenzione di chi osserva le contraddizioni del presente, le tensioni di una contemporaneità che assiste alla minaccia del ritorno dei totalitarismi e alle derive autoritarie che si fanno strada sempre più insistentemente. In questo contesto, l’artista tratta tematiche quali censura, centralità del linguaggio e controllo dei media operato dai governi e lo fa con opere come SoundOnMySkin , display a lettere rotanti che sconfessa il proprio ruolo di mezzo indicato per dotare le persone di informazioni chiare e, invece, fornisce frasi sconnesse, confuse.

In entrambe le opere, è il linguaggio ad essere indagato. Primo baluardo delle democrazie che, oggi più che mai, è utilizzato da governi e regimi come mezzo per orientare popoli sempre più provati dalle sfide del presente. Nel percorso figurano anche installazioni interattive quali Stand, Speak, Here (realizzata nel 2026) e Breathe che, tramite modalità differenti, invitano i visitatori a confrontarsi direttamente con esse. La prima ci esorta a salire su dei mattoni ed emettere un suono con le labbra chiuse, chiaro riferimento alla marginalizzazione e alla repressione del dissenso nel discorso politico. La seconda chiama invece all’azione il visitatore, a cui viene offerta la possibilità di realizzare un frottage appoggiando un foglio di carta sulle incisioni fatte dall’artista su una parete del museo per poi ricalcare con il pastello. Nelle scene incise si nota subito la mancanza dei manifestanti arrestati. Gupta mostra deliberatamente solo le figure delle forze dell’ordine o degli abusanti, mentre i profili dei dissidenti compaiono solo attraverso l’eco della loro assenza.

Il progetto della GAM nasce all’interno di una collaborazione che dal 2021 lega Fondazione Furla e il museo milanese. Ogni anno la partnership produce una mostra inedita pensata per far dialogare la ricerca di un’artista contemporanea con gli ambienti storici della GAM e con la sua collezione. È un confronto che permette di leggere le opere anche attraverso la distanza, temporale e culturale, che le separa dalle opere conservate nel museo. Furla Series , avviato nel 2017 da Fondazione Furla in collaborazione con importanti istituzioni artistiche italiane, ha dato vita a mostre personali di artiste da tutto il mondo e ha contribuito a offrire visibilità alle donne protagoniste della cultura contemporanea. L’appuntamento milanese con Shilpa Gupta si inserisce in una ricerca artistica di ampio respiro internazionale. Dalla Biennale di Venezia alle biennali di Berlino, Sharjah, Liverpool e Gwangju, fino alle mostre nei musei di Europa, Asia e Stati Uniti, il lavoro dell’artista ha attraversato contesti diversi mantenendo sempre al centro il rapporto tra individuo, territorio e strutture di potere.
excerpt_original: Fino al 6 gennaio 2027, gli spazi del museo milanese ospitano le opere di Shilpa Gupta con One Palm Closer to the Sky, mostra curata da Bruna Roccasalva e promossa da Fondazione Furla e GAM L'articolo Shilpa Gupta, il linguaggio come spazio di libertà alla GAM di Milano proviene…

editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/47a2134e/678d6fc2-c65d-459d-92c0-f3b3f27f3ea8.png?w=2352&q=70&fm=webp", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "以“INTO THE EMOTIONS ～感动之入口～”为理念于2017年创办的设计与艺术节“DESIGNART TOKYO”将以银座的KK线（东京高速道路）为主会场，于10月30日至11月8日举办。迎来第10届的今年，主题为“Hibiki”。设计、艺术、室内设计、时尚、科技等丰富多彩类别的展览将在都内约70处地点展开。此外，在银座、有乐町地区的“KK线”内，将由锐意进取的建筑设计工作室“ALTEMY”呈现造型感的临时建筑。该建筑将作为约4000平方米的大规模主会场“AUTOBAHN / KK线”闪亮登场。观众不仅可以欣赏从国内外汇聚的大量展品，还可以尽情体验能购买作品的市集、可供餐饮的PARK & CAFÉ以及每天在舞台上举行的讲座活动等各种区域。", "links": [{"text": "「DESIGNART TOKYO」", "url": "https://www.tokyoartbeat.com/events/-/Designart-Tokyo-2026/KK-Line-Tokyo-Expressway/2026-10-30"}, {"text": "KK線（東京高速道路）", "url": "https://www.tokyoartbeat.com/venues/-/KK-Line-Tokyo-Expressway"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://cdn.prod.tabdev.net/asset_files/uploaded/2026-10/753aef8e/Authobarn .png?q=70&fm=webp", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Tokyo Art Beat", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们将向Tokyo Art Beat的付费会员独家抽奖赠送主会场“AUTOBAHN / KK线”的入场门票（1日票），共计10组20人。1日票可在主会场举办期间的10月30日至11月3日中的任意一天使用。每天最多可入场3次。营业时间 10:00～19:00（请注意，首日和最后一天的开闭馆时间有所不同） ※首日10月30日从12:00开始可以入场。 ※10月30日至11月2日的一般最后入场时间为18:00。 ※11月3日的一般最后入场时间为16:00。 ※活动当天可能会对活动现场进行采访与拍摄，观众的影像可能会被刊登于各种媒体、网站、社交媒体等。敬请提前谅解。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "报名方法", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在报名表单中填写必要事项 期限：10月9日～10月23日 23:59 👉点击此处填写报名表 ＊预计于10月中旬向中奖者寄送奖品 ＊门票将通过电子邮件发送。 ＊报名申请已截止。感谢您的踊跃报名。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
「INTO THE EMOTIONS ～感動の入口～」をコンセプトに、2017年にスタートしたデザイン＆アートフェスティバル 「DESIGNART TOKYO」 が銀座の KK線（東京高速道路） をメイン会場として、10月30日から11月8日まで開催されます。10回目を迎える今年のテーマは「Hibiki」。デザイン、アート、インテリア、ファッション、テクノロジーなど、多彩なジャンルの展示を都内約70ヶ所で行われます。 また銀座・有楽町エリアの「KK線」内には、気鋭の建築デザインスタジオ「ALTEMY」による造形的な仮設建築を展開。約4000平米の大規模メイン会場「AUTOBAHN / KK線」として登場します。国内外から集結した多数の展示作品だけでなく、作品を購入できるマーケットや飲食もできるPARK & CAFÉ、毎日ステージで行われるトークイベントなど、様々なエリアを楽しむことができます。

メイン会場「AUTOBAHN / KK線」の入場チケット（1日券）を Tokyo Art Beatの有料会員限定で、抽選で10組20名様にプレゼント します。 1日券はメイン会場の開催期間10月30日から11月3日まで、どの日でもお入りいただけます。1日につき3回まで入場可能です。 営業時間 10:00〜19:00（初日と最終日はオープン・クローズ時間が異なりますのでご注意ください） ※初日の10月30日は12:00から入場可能です。 ※10月30日から11月2日の一般最終入場は18:00です。 ※11月3日は一般最終入場16:00です。 ※当日はイベントの模様を取材・撮影する可能性があり、お客様の様子が各種メディア媒体、Webサイト、ソーシャルメディア等に掲載される場合がございます。あらかじめご了承ください。

応募方法

応募フォームに必要事項を記入 期間：10月9日〜10月23日 23:59 👉応募フォームはこちら ＊当選者への発送は10月中を予定しています ＊チケットはメールにてお送りいたします。 ＊お申し込みの受付を終了いたしました。ご応募ありがとうございました。

title_original: Tokyo Opener ‘Sukiyaki’ Director Zeze Takahisa on the Protest Roots of a Global Japanese Pop Hit: ‘The Culture Used to Be Wide Open – Now It’s Become Narrower’
editorial_title_zh: 东京电影节开幕片《Sukiyaki》导演濑濑敬久谈全球日本流行金曲背后的抗争根源：“过去文化是完全敞开的——现在却变得狭隘了”
editorial_excerpt_zh: 作为第39届东京国际电影节的开幕影片，濑濑敬久的《Sukiyaki》讲述了同名歌曲如何在1963年成为全球热门金曲，以及它如何成为一首备受喜爱的经典之作，其外语翻唱版本也曾登上各大排行榜。这部...
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "作为第39届东京国际电影节的开幕影片，濑濑敬久的《Sukiyaki》讲述了同名歌曲如何在1963年成为全球热门金曲，以及它如何成为一首备受喜爱的经典之作，其外语翻唱版本也曾登上各大排行榜。", "links": [{"text": "Tokyo International Film Festival", "url": "https://variety.com/t/tokyo-international-film-festival/"}, {"text": "Zeze Takahisa", "url": "https://variety.com/t/zeze-takahisa/"}, {"text": "Sukiyaki", "url": "https://variety.com/t/sukiyaki/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "影片不仅停留在歌曲本身，还深入探究了创作者的生活与职业生涯：作词人永六辅（松坂桃李饰）、作曲人中村八大（冈田准星饰）以及歌手坂本九（仲野太贺饰）。他们在日本被称为“689三人组”，这个不寻常的绰号源自他们名字中的“数字”汉字：八（8）、六（6）和九（9）。但正如影片在一场又一场充满张力的戏剧化场景中所展现的那样，他们之间的职业与个人关系并非总是一帆风顺。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "相关报道", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/snl-uk-.jpg?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "截图", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "英国《周六夜现场》开场短剧上演威廉王子与凯特、哈里王子与梅根的重聚（在安德鲁前王子的一些帮助下）：“他们一定想让我们重新成为王室成员！”", "links": [{"text": "'SNL U.K.' Cold Open Sees Reunion Between Prince William and Kate and Prince Harry and Meghan (With Some Help From Former Prince Andrew): 'They Must Want Us to Be Royals Again!'", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/tv/global/snl-uk-prince-william-kate-reunite-prince-harry-meghan-1236908054/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://variety.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/meghan.jpg?w=250&h=167&crop=1", "alt": "澳大利亚墨尔本 - 4月14日：萨塞克斯公爵夫人梅根与妇女无家可归者及家庭暴力庇护所麦考利社区服务中心的员工于2026年4月14日在澳大利亚墨尔本富茨克雷郊区为居民提供午餐。梅根与萨塞克斯公爵哈里正在澳大利亚进行为期四天的访问，行程涵盖墨尔本、堪培拉和悉尼。（摄影：Jonathan Brady-Pool/Getty Images）", "caption": "", "credit": "Variety · Film", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "梅根·马克尔将联手主持《澳大利亚少年厨神》", "links": [{"text": "Meghan Markle to Co-Host 'Junior MasterChef Australia'", "url": "https://variety.com/2026/tv/global/meghan-markle-co-host-junior-masterchef-australia-1236931967/"}], "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在影片日本发行商东宝的总部接受采访时，濑濑强调了这部电影在“Sukiyaki”（当地名为《上を向いて歩こう》即《昂首向前走》）首次登上排行榜六十年后的现实意义。“当时这个国家正从战争中恢复，来自海外的各种影响如潮水般涌入，”濑濑说道。“这些影响创造了一种推动这里流行文化的能量。现在日本从海外吸收的影响变少了。过去文化是完全敞开的——现在却变得狭隘了。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但如今，日本年轻人正在重新发掘昭和时代（1926-1989，即昭和天皇统治时期）那种能量，当时日本流行文化正处于硕果累累的巅峰。与怀旧的婴儿潮一代一样，他们也出现在《哥斯拉-1.0》的观众席中——这部设定在战后初期的2023年轰动一时的哥斯拉系列电影。导演山崎贵执导的续集《哥斯拉-0.0》也作为本届东京电影节的焦点展映亮相，“这算是一种昭和热潮吧，”濑濑半开玩笑地说。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "谈到《Sukiyaki》的选角时，他说主要的标准并不是长相与主要人物相似，尽管中野太贺以惊人的精准度演绎了坂本九那充满感染力的舞台形象。“这更多是关于演员所投射出的感觉，”濑濑解释道。“但太贺出身于有电影时代根基的演艺世家，因此他对这个角色有着天然的亲近感。此外，当坂本九在片中唱歌时，你听到的是太贺的声音——他作为歌手有着惊人的天赋。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "不过，影片的剧情更多地集中在中村和永六辅身上，他们在20世纪60年代联手创作了一系列热门歌曲，但随着中村陷入酗酒而发生争吵并分道扬镳。“中村在《Sukiyaki》大火之后经历了一段艰难时期，所以我们将这一点展现了出来，”濑濑说道。“如果这部电影仅仅是一个成功的故事，那它就不会有趣——它必须既有高潮也有低谷。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "所有这些戏剧性事件其实与《Sukiyaki》在海外走红并没有太大关系，但影片同样深入探讨了其创作的源头，从中村对爵士钢琴的精湛掌握（他在纽约俱乐部中展露过这一才华），到坂本九对早期摇滚乐的根基（他是埃尔维斯的超级粉丝），再到永六辅对饱含深情的日本歌词的创作，", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“当然，海外的人听不懂歌词，但歌曲中的能量传达给了他们，”濑濑说。“歌词反映了当时日本正在发生的事情。”词作家永六辅的灵感来自于1960年反对此美日安保条约的游行示威。“示威者呼吁和平，但没能阻止条约的批准。”濑濑说道，“尽管他们失败了，但他还是希望他们能够‘昂首阔步’。因此这首歌很有深度——它不仅仅是一首欢快的流行曲调。”", "translated": true}]

article_text:
The opening film of the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival , Zeze Takahisa ’s “ Sukiyaki ” tells the story of how the title tune became a worldwide hit in 1963 as well as a beloved standard that has been recorded in foreign-language versions that have also topped charts.

The film goes beyond the song itself to delve into the lives and careers of its makers: lyricist Ei Roksuke (Matsuzaka Tori), composer Nakamura Hachidai (Okada Junichi), and singer Sakamoto Kyu (Nakano Taiga). They became known in Japan as the “689 trio” with the unusual moniker coming from the “number” characters in their names: Hachi (8), Roku (6) and Kyu (9). But as the film shows in scene after highly charged dramatic scene, their professional and personal relationships were not always harmonious.

Interviewed at the headquarters of Toho, the film’s Japan distributor, Zeze stressed the film’s relevance, six decades after “Sukiyaki,” known locally as “Ue o Muite Aruko” (I’ll Walk with My Head Up”), first hit the charts. “Back then the country was recovering from the war and all sorts of influences were flooding in from abroad,” Zeze said. “Those influences created an energy that propelled the popular culture here. Now Japan is absorbing fewer influences from abroad. The culture used to be wide open – now it’s become narrower.”

But younger Japanese are now discovering that energy from the Showa Era (1926-1989), the period of Emperor Showa’s reign, when Japanese pop culture was at a fertile peak. Together with nostalgic Boomers, they could be found in the audience of “Godzilla Minus One,” the 2023 smash hit Godzilla series installment set in the early postwar period . The follow-up by director Yamazaki Takashi, “Godzilla Minus Zero” is also at TIFF as the festival’s Centerpiece screening, “It’s a kind of Showa boom,” joked Zeze.

In casting “Sukiyaki,” he says, the main criterion was not a physical resemblance to its main characters, though Nakano Taiga channels Sakamoto’s exuberant stage persona with an uncanny precision. “It was more about the feeling the actors projected,” Zeze explains. “But Taiga comes from a show business family with roots in film’s period so he had a natural affinity for the role. Also, when Sakamoto sings in the film, it’s Taiga’s voice you’re hearing – he has an amazing talent as a vocalist.”

The film’s drama, though, centers more on Nakamura and Ei, who joined forces to compose a series of hits in the 1960s but quarreled and parted as Nakamura spiraled into alcoholism. “ Nakamura went through a tough period after ‘Sukiyaki’ became a hit so we show that,” says Zeze. “If the film were just a success story, it wouldn’t be interesting – it has to have both ups and downs.”

None of this drama had much to do with “Sukiyaki” becoming a hit abroad, but the film also delves into the sources of its creation, from Nakamura’s mastery of the jazz piano, which he displayed in New York clubs, to Sakamoto’s roots into early rock – he was a big Elvis fan – and Ei’s composition of the poignant Japanese lyrics,

“Of course people abroad didn’t understand the lyrics, but the song’s energy came across to them,” says Zeze. “The lyrics reflect what was happening in Japan at that time.” Ei Rokusuke, the lyricist, was inspired by the demonstrations against the Japan-US Security Treaty in 1960. “ The demonstrators called for peace, but failed to stop the treaty ratification. “He wanted them to ‘walk with their heads up,’ despite their defeat,” says Zeze. “So the song has depth – it ‘s not just a cheery pop tune.”

"credit": "Film Comment", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《掩盖》（劳拉·波伊特拉斯与马克·奥本豪斯，2025）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "身处威尼斯电影节，有一种奇特的镇静感。一年一度的威尼斯国际艺术电影节并非在威尼斯本岛举行，而是在一座名为利多的小岛上，从大陆乘渡轮15分钟即可抵达。对我这样的纽约人来说，如果说威尼斯像一场模拟——铺砌的无车道路、如画般的运河、历史悠久的建筑立面——那么利多则像是世界边缘之外的田园牧歌。这里曾是“浴疗度假”与温泉小镇，岛上弥漫着潮湿的慵懒——即便电影节喧嚣热闹，将超过100,000名访客带到这个约20,000人的社区，它仍显得疏朗而缓慢。我听着教堂钟声的报时，决定何时动身去看一场放映。我在公寓里趁两部电影之间的空隙小睡。当我意识到晚上10点后几乎不可能买到食物时，我便用从小夫妻店买来的杂货自己做饭。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "如果这一切都令人非常放松，它也多少令人麻木，而挤满电影节主竞赛单元的、志在获奖、明星云集、情节公式化的影片对此毫无帮助。无论是保罗·索伦蒂诺的开幕片《恩典》，片中托尼·塞尔维洛饰演一位意大利总统，正与一部安乐死法律（以及一位留着脏辫的黑人教皇的不赞同）角力；还是约戈斯·兰斯莫斯的《毒菌》，一部肮脏癫狂的惊悚片，讲述两个被QAnon洗脑的incel式人物绑架了一位萨克勒式的CEO；抑或凯瑟琳·毕格罗平淡无味的《炸药之屋》，追踪美国政府战情室内部的运作，一枚核导弹（由一个恰好身份不明的敌人发射）正朝该国飞驰而来——许多竞赛单元的叙事似乎都在竭力追求现实相关性，却像游乐场幻想般展开：人物刻画粗疏、自我放纵得令人恼火，缺乏有意义的利害关系。（吉姆·贾木许赢得金狮奖的《父亲母亲姐妹兄弟》和吉尔莫·德尔·托罗的《弗兰肯斯坦》是两个例外——前者因其对亲子关系优美敏锐而机智的探索，后者因其对玛丽·雪莱存在主义毫不掩饰的歌剧式拥抱。）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "也许正因如此，我在今年电影节上最珍视的影片主要来自非竞赛单元，且或多或少属于非虚构作品，它们以现实的闪电刺穿了利多虚幻的泡沫。证据A：劳拉·波伊特拉斯与马克·奥本豪斯的纪录片《掩盖》。这部影片讲述的是著名而执着的美国调查记者西摩·赫什，尽管“讲述”在这里似乎是个错误的介词。波伊特拉斯的几部影片都从一个人的生活与工作出发——爱德华·斯诺登、朱利安·阿桑奇、南·戈尔丁——但只是将其作为结构性原则，以探索具有更广泛社会和政治意义的观念与议题。她的纪录片避开了当代非虚构作品中两种令人恼火的潮流——名人传记片和大量蒙太奇堆砌的议题片——以触及某种远为鲜活动人的东西：一种个体如何在历史中定位自身的感觉。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "就赫什而言，这段历史漫长而艰难。对认识他的人来说，西（Sy）的职业生涯始于向权力说真话，他报道了1968年越南的美莱村屠杀，美国士兵以打击越共为借口，残忍杀害了数百名手无寸铁的儿童和成人——有时是先强奸和残害他们。 《掩盖》以赫什讲述那则独家新闻如何产生开场，强调它并不需要多少硬核侦探技巧：事实就明摆在眼前，却没有人主动去调查或报道。这种对消极与共谋的直面，成为一条贯穿线，连接着波伊特拉斯和奥本豪斯让赫什带我们走过的许多故事——一长串国家认可的罪行——包括“混乱行动”，即中央情报局在1960年代监视学生抗议者的秘密计划；水门事件；以及阿布格莱布监狱的黑暗揭露。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "波伊特拉斯和奥本豪斯的风格简单直接，且暗藏论战性。尽管赫什的故事主要通过档案材料和采访讲述，我们仍能瞥见他与加沙一位消息人士交谈的间歇场景，谈及以色列国防军杀害儿童；与美莱村的呼应难以忽视。在采访片段中，常能听到波伊特拉斯的声音温和地探问这位棘手的赫什，他害怕暴露消息来源，也不愿拍一部以他而非他的报道对象为中心的影片；他只简短地谈及自己的个人生活、婚姻或子女。他努力抵制那种将历史性和系统性斗争简化为简单英雄-反派叙事的个人化与英雄化，其中有一种非凡的真诚——这种努力被波伊特拉斯和奥本豪斯的导演与剪辑置于前景。我走出影院时对赫什心怀敬畏，但更重要的是，我想起了先于我们当下、并必须不减地延续到未来的漫长正义斗争。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "卢克蕾西娅·马特尔（Lucrecia Martel）在《地标》（Landmarks，西班牙语片名 Nuestra tierra，意为“我们的土地”）中同样兼顾了长远的视野与切近的视角、历史与个人，这是她的首部纪录长片。影片以2009年68岁的原住民活动人士哈维尔·乔科巴尔（Javier Chocobar）被杀害为起点，当时他与警察和一名试图将丘斯查加斯塔（Chuschagasta）社群成员逐出其在阿根廷图库曼省祖传土地的地主发生对峙。尽管这一事件被录像拍下，案件却用了九年才进入法庭；凶手被定罪并羁押，但因法院迟迟未审理其上诉，于2020年获释。马特尔追踪了这场审判的法律程序，其中包括公开听证与情景重现。但她谨慎地将镜头扩展到这一单一事件之外——这一事件因法律程序的拖沓与复杂化，有可能掩盖阿根廷殖民主义长期而持续的不公。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "马特尔与联合编剧玛丽亚·阿尔切（María Alché）深入挖掘这片土地被殖民与归属的历史，详述了种种盗窃与法律上的障眼法，它们构成了这看似孤立的暴力行为的脚手架。她们这一做法的意义在一个关键时刻得以显现：法庭上，被告援引一位作家的一篇文章，声称丘斯查加斯塔社群已于1807年灭绝。马特尔采访了这位作家，他震惊地意识到自己的作品产生了现实后果；他说自己只是为了一篇关于拍卖的文章“增添趣味”才写了那些东西，而如果他每天写的东西都要去查证，他“会死”。这里关乎的是一场集体记忆之战，而《地标》清楚表明，档案是一种结构，其设计就是为了让某些社群凌驾于其他社群之上。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "有些人可能会觉得影片中段——丘斯查加斯塔社群成员接受采访、讲述各自家族史的部分——对于一位以大胆风格实验著称的导演来说，直白得令人意外。但这种直白强化了我对整部影片的印象：这是一部致力于为那些常被刻意抹去的生命留下记录的影片。这些场景与官方程序形成了有力的对照——在官方程序中，文件、契约和法律是国家行使其霸权的手段。影片中有一个富有诗意的处理：无人机镜头贯穿全片，既令人联想到监视，也唤起一种幽灵般的感觉——这片土地先于我们在银幕上看到的任何人而存在，它见证了甚至早于阿根廷这个国家存在的生命。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "突尼斯导演考塞尔·本·哈尼亚（Kaouther Ben Hania）的《欣德·拉贾卜的声音》（The Voice of Hind Rajab）同样聚焦于官僚机构所谓中立运作中固有的暴力——即规则与程序的暴政。该片获得了本届电影节的评审团大奖。欣德·拉贾卜是一名5岁的巴勒斯坦女孩，2024年1月，她的亲属在试图乘车撤离加沙时被以色列国防军枪杀。拉贾卜被困在车内，周围是他们的尸体，她用手机致电巴勒斯坦红新月会求助。她与红新月会工作人员通话的录音令人肝肠寸断，她在其中恳求他们前来营救，而工作人员则无助地寻求批准派救护车前去援助她——这些录音构成了本·哈尼亚影片的核心。导演使用了拉贾卜通话的真实音频，但用演员重构了红新月会呼叫中心里发生的情景。影片展开的方式像一出注定悲剧的室内剧，结局缓慢却必然地到来：救护车距离拉贾卜仅咫尺之遥时，士兵们开枪打死了这个小女孩和两名救援人员。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这部影片在许多影评人中引发了质疑，而且理由充分。本·哈尼亚是与拉贾卜的母亲和家人合作拍摄此片的，然而，将一名儿童的遇害戏剧化——她只是在这场仍在持续的屠杀中不断被杀害的众多儿童之一——带有剥削的恶臭，而影片参与一个大型欧洲电影节光鲜竞赛单元更强化了这种感觉。许多好莱坞明星和电影人作为执行制片人在这部影片上署名，包括鲁妮·玛拉、乔纳森·格雷泽、华金·菲尼克斯和布拉德·皮特，这促使社交媒体上的人们发问：为什么拉贾卜的母亲至今仍未从加沙撤离？我带着这些保留意见走进影片，尽管影片并未完全消除它们，但我走出影院时，确实被本·哈尼亚的处理方式所打动。",
